Ken Block

Independent candidate for Governor, Rhode Island · Open seat

Software engineer and business owner. His firm works with governments and businesses to cut unnecessary spending.

Ken Block, 61, of Barrington, is a software engineer and government watchdog who announced an independent run for Rhode Island governor on April 2, 2026. This is his third run for governor: he ran in 2010 as the nominee of the Moderate Party, which he founded, and in 2014 as a Republican. He is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot with Democrat Helena Buonanno Foulkes and Republican Aaron Guckian.

Where Block stands

Taxes
Says he would veto a millionaires tax if the legislature passed one. Says his aim is to cut expenses, not add taxes, and that a $15 billion budget should be enough.
Energy
Proposes cutting government-imposed charges on home and business electric bills. Would move necessary taxes off electric bills to what he calls fairer, more transparent ways of raising revenue.
Truck tolls
Would suspend the state's truck-toll program and says he would veto any move to toll passenger vehicles.
Housing
Supports reviewing state-owned land and buildings for affordable housing and requiring a 'Housing Note' on bills showing their impact on housing. In the final debate he gave a range of 10,000 to 30,000 new homes and stressed simpler permitting.
Housing mandates
Supports simpler permitting and regulation for developers, with buy-in from cities and towns. Says solar projects are taking thousands of acres of land that could be used for housing.
State pensions (retiree COLAs)
Would restore cost-of-living increases for people who retired before 2012. Proposes paying for them with excess pension-fund investment earnings rather than state tax revenue.
State spending
Says the state budget has nearly doubled in ten years. Proposes reviewing the operations, systems and staffing of every state agency, and called the Republican nominee's plan to cut $1.5 billion a 'fantasy.'
Judicial selection
Says judicial selection is still highly political and would make merit the priority in appointments. Would move magistrate appointments away from the General Assembly to the same process used for judges.
Transparency / tax returns
Has declined to release his 2025 tax returns. He says his small business's pass-through filings could help competitors, and that he has 'been plenty transparent.'
Sports betting
Said yes when asked in the final debate whether the state should reexamine its sports betting laws.

Background

  • Software engineer; owns a firm that helps governments and businesses reduce spending
  • Founded Rhode Island's Moderate Party
  • Moderate Party nominee for governor, 2010 (lost)
  • Ran for governor as a Republican, 2014 (lost)
  • Wrote a book on his analysis of 2020 election voter-fraud claims
  • Pushed for a line-item veto, a state inspector general and removing the 'master lever' from ballots
  • Independent candidate for governor, 2026
